name: process.shell
description: Spawn a process via ShellExecuteEx. Handles paths with spaces / unicode without shell-escape hazards, supports non-default Win32 verbs (runas for elevation, print, edit, explore). Pass `wait_for_window_ms` to also wait for the new process's first window.

path.description: Absolute path to the file / executable / URL / shell item. ShellExecuteEx handles document-launch semantics — `.txt` opens in Notepad, `.url` follows the link, etc.

args.description: Parameter string passed verbatim to the spawned program. Optional. Used as ShellExecuteEx's lpParameters.

verb.description: Win32 shell verb. `open` (default): standard launch. `runas`: elevate via UAC consent prompt (interactive). `print`: send to default printer. `edit`: open in editor. `explore`: open Explorer at the path. `find`: open search rooted at the path.

cwd.description: Working directory for the new process. Defaults to the agent's cwd.

wait_for_window_ms.description: When greater than 0, block until the first of: a matching window appears (returns `window`); the process exits (returns `window_timeout: true` and `exit_code`); or this many milliseconds pass (returns `window_timeout: true`). A matching window is owned by the new pid, has no owner window, and passes the same filter as `window.list` (visible, non-empty title, not a tool or no-activate window, non-zero size, on a monitor). An app with a splash screen returns the splash screen. Browsers that hand off to an already-running instance return on process exit. 0 or omitted: return immediately, as before. Ignored when no process spawns (`pid: null`); none of the window fields are returned then.

pid.description: Process id of the spawned process, or `null` when no process spawns (e.g. `print` on a file that opens in an existing handler instance). Caller must null-check before passing to process.kill / process.wait (both of which require pid >= 1).

window.description: Present only when `wait_for_window_ms` > 0 and a matching window appeared.

handle.description: Window handle in `win:0x<hex>` form, as in `window.list`.

title.description: Window title when it was matched.

window_timeout.description: Present (always `true`) only when `wait_for_window_ms` > 0 and no window matched, because the process exited or the time ran out. Absent when `window` is present.

exit_code.description: Present only with `window_timeout` when the wait ended because the process exited.

x-implementations.name: shell_execute_ex_w
x-implementations.description: Win32 `ShellExecuteExW` (Unicode) with SEE_MASK_NOCLOSEPROCESS to retrieve the spawned process handle for pid extraction.

x-implementations.name: shell_execute_ex_a
x-implementations.description: Win32 `ShellExecuteExA` legacy fallback for NT 4 / 9x. ANSI strings transcoded by the agent.

windows-modern.description: ShellExecuteExW. `verb: runas` triggers UAC consent — interactive prompt blocks the agent until the user responds. `user_cancelled` ERR if the user denies the prompt. `no_handler` when no application is registered for the path's file association. With wait_for_window_ms, the agent keeps the SEE_MASK_NOCLOSEPROCESS handle open for the duration of the wait and returns on window, exit or timeout.

windows-classic.description: ShellExecuteExW on NT 5+; ShellExecuteExA on NT 4 / 9x. `runas` is NT 5+ — pre-NT-5 returns ERR not_supported. NT 4 lacks UAC; `runas` simply uses RunAs Service when present, else errors. With wait_for_window_ms, the agent keeps the SEE_MASK_NOCLOSEPROCESS handle open for the duration of the wait and returns on window, exit or timeout.
